questions.question: A bag has 6 red balls and 2 blue balls. Is picking red more likely or less likely than picking blue?
questions.explain: There are 6 red and only 2 blue, so red has the bigger group and is more likely. A common mix-up is to call two different groups equally likely just because there are two colours.

questions.question: A bag has 7 red balls and 3 blue balls. Sam says red and blue are equally likely. Is Sam right?
questions.explain: Red has 7 and blue has 3, so red is more likely. The trap is to think that two colours must always have the same chance, no matter how many of each there are.

questions.question: A bag has 10 purple balls and no pink balls. Is picking purple more likely, less likely, or the same as picking pink?
questions.explain: There are 10 purple and zero pink, so purple is more likely. Pink cannot come out at all. Do not call two different groups 'the same' just because both names are in the bag.

questions.question: A bag has 2 red balls and 8 blue balls. Is picking red more likely or less likely than picking blue?
questions.explain: Red has 2 and blue has 8, so red is less likely. A common mistake is to swap more and less, or to say two groups are the same when the numbers are different.

questions.question: Mia has a bag with 5 red marbles and 3 blue marbles for her game. Is picking red more likely or less likely than picking blue?
questions.explain: 5 red is bigger than 3 blue, so red is more likely. Remember to compare the sizes of the groups, not just count how many colours there are.

questions.question: There is a spinner with 2 big red sections and 2 small blue sections. Jay spins it. Is landing on red more likely, less likely, or the same as landing on blue?
questions.explain: The red sections are bigger, so red is more likely even though both colours have 2 sections. Counting sections without looking at their size is a common trap.

questions.question: Max has a bag with 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. His friend picks one. Is getting blue more likely or less likely than getting red?
questions.explain: Blue has 6 and red has 4, so blue is more likely. If you see two different numbers, the bigger group is more likely, not the same.

questions.question: A bag has some red balls and 5 blue balls. Picking red is more likely than picking blue. How many red balls are in the bag?
questions.explain: Red must have more than 5 to be more likely, so 7 works. Picking 5 makes them the same, and picking fewer makes red less likely.

questions.question: A spinner has 1 big red section, 1 medium blue section, and 1 small green section. Is red more likely, less likely, or the same as green?
questions.explain: The red section is big and the green section is small, so red is more likely. The trap is to think three sections mean three equal chances without checking their sizes.

questions.question: A bag has 6 red balls and 6 blue balls. Mom adds 2 more blue balls. Now is picking blue more likely, less likely, or the same as picking red?
questions.explain: After adding 2 blue, the bag has 6 red and 8 blue, so blue is now more likely. The trap is to remember the original 6 and 6 and forget the 2 extra balls.

questions.question: At the school fair, a bag holds 9 green tickets and 4 orange tickets. Nina picks one ticket without looking. Is picking green more likely or less likely than picking orange?
options: Less likely, there are more green
Equally likely, it has two colours
More likely, there are more green
Equally likely, both can be picked
questions.explain: There are 9 green tickets and only 4 orange, so green is more likely. Having more of a colour gives a better chance, not a worse one.

questions.question: Kim spins a spinner in a board game. One big blue section covers most of the spinner, and 3 tiny yellow sections fill the rest. Is landing on blue more likely or less likely than landing on yellow?
options: Less likely, blue is one part
questions.explain: Blue takes up most of the spinner, so the arrow lands on blue more often. Counting sections is not enough — look at how much space each colour covers.

questions.question: Ivy's craft bag holds 3 red buttons and 11 white buttons. She pulls out one button without looking. Is picking red more likely or less likely than picking white?
questions.explain: Only 3 buttons are red and 11 are white, so red is less likely. Fewer of a colour means a smaller chance, not a bigger one.

questions.question: Ravi has a bag of red and blue marbles for a game. He wants to know which colour is more likely to be picked. What should he do?
options: Count how many colours he has
Count how many of each colour
Say two colours are the same
Pick the colour with fewer balls
questions.explain: To compare, count the red marbles and the blue marbles. The colour with more marbles is the more likely one; how many colours there are does not matter.

questions.question: A bag has 8 green cubes and 3 red cubes. Ali takes 6 green cubes out of the bag. Now is picking green more likely or less likely than picking red?
options: Equally likely, both are still in
questions.explain: 8 green take away 6 leaves 2 green, and there are 3 red, so green is now less likely. Compare the numbers after the change, not before.

questions.question: Nora's bag has 8 white beads and some black beads. Picking black is more likely than picking white. What is the smallest number of black beads that works?
questions.explain: Black must be more than 8 to be more likely, so 9 is the smallest. With 8 and 8 the two colours would be equally likely instead.

questions.question: A spinner has 1 large orange section that covers most of the circle. The rest is 3 tiny grey sections. Max says grey is more likely because grey has 3 sections. What is wrong with what Max said?
options: Both are the same, 2 colours spin
Orange is 1 part, so it is less
Grey has 3 parts, so Max is right
questions.explain: The arrow lands where there is the most space, and orange fills most of the spinner. Three tiny parts are still a small space, so counting parts can fool you.

questions.question: Bag A has 5 red and 2 white marbles. Bag B has 3 red and 6 white marbles. Ava wants the best chance of picking red. Which bag should she use?
options: Bag B, it has fewer red ones
Bag A, red beats white there
questions.explain: In Bag A red (5) is more than white (2), so red is more likely there. In Bag B red (3) is less than white (6), so red is less likely.
